title: AI Daily Brief - 2026-06-07
tags:
  - applied-ai
---

## Today in One Minute

- Google released Gemma 4 QAT models, smaller compressed versions that run more efficiently on laptops and mobile devices.
- OpenAI introduced "Dreaming", a new memory feature that gives ChatGPT better recall across conversations.
- Utah State has rolled out Gemini for Education to all its K-12 schools, signalling a wider classroom shift to integrated AI tools.

## What Happened

- Google published Gemma 4 with Quantization-Aware Training (QAT). The technique trains the model knowing it will later be compressed, so the smaller version keeps more of the quality of the full model while needing less memory and battery. Google positions it for everyday laptops and phones.
- OpenAI announced "Dreaming", an upgrade to ChatGPT memory. The system processes past conversations in the background to form more useful long-term context, so ChatGPT can remember user preferences and prior work more reliably.
- Google announced a partnership with the State of Utah to bring Gemini for Education to every K-12 school in the state, including teacher tools, lesson support, and student-facing features with age-appropriate safeguards.

## Why It Matters

- A capable local model that runs well on a Windows 11 laptop means lecturers and students can experiment with AI offline, without paying for cloud usage and without sending sensitive coursework to external servers.
- Better ChatGPT memory changes how students and staff plan, draft, and revise work over time. It also raises real concerns about what gets remembered, what should be deleted, and what counts as the student's own thinking.
- A whole-state K-12 rollout is a clear signal that students entering RP diplomas will increasingly arrive already used to AI-assisted learning. Our teaching needs to assume baseline AI fluency and focus on judgement, verification, and applied skill.

## Try This Today

- Download a small Gemma model through a local runner such as LM Studio or Ollama on your Windows 11 laptop, ask it to summarise a lecture outline, and compare the answer to the same prompt run in ChatGPT or Gemini online.
- In ChatGPT, open Settings then Personalization, and review what is currently saved in Memory. Delete anything outdated or sensitive, then ask ChatGPT to summarise what it "knows" about you and check if it matches your expectations.
- Write a 3-line prompt that an incoming Year 1 student might use to "do their homework" for one of your modules, then list two checks you would add to the assignment brief to make sure the student still demonstrates real understanding.

## Teaching Angle

- Run a 10-minute classroom demo comparing a small local Gemma model on a laptop versus a large cloud model on the same task. Ask students to spot differences in accuracy, speed, and which use cases each is suitable for.
- Hold a short discussion on AI memory using the new ChatGPT "Dreaming" feature: what are the benefits for long projects, and what are the privacy risks if a student logs in on a shared lab PC? Ask each group to draft one classroom rule for using AI memory responsibly.
- Use the Utah K-12 rollout as a starting point for a reflection activity. Ask students how their secondary school used (or did not use) AI, and what they expect from AI support in a diploma module. Use the answers to shape your own AI ground rules for the semester.

## Links

- [Gemma 4 QAT models: Optimizing model compression for mobile and laptop efficiency](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/quantization-aware-training-gemma-4/)
- [Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-memory-dreaming)
- [Utah State brings Gemini for Education to all K-12 schools](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/education/utah-state-education-partnership/)
